Query packed indexes

Source: R/index.R
geo_query_box.Rd

geo_query_box() finds the indexed geometries whose boxes intersect each query box. geo_query_radius() finds the points of a k-d tree within a distance. geo_query_nearest() finds up to k geometries of an R-tree by box distance, nearest first; a box distance can be smaller than the distance between the geometries, so these are candidates that GEOS or S2 can refine. geo_join_box() pairs every box of y with the indexed boxes it intersects, in one call; when y is itself an R-tree both trees are descended together (design section 6.8).

Usage

geo_query_box(index, extent)

geo_query_radius(index, x, y, r)

geo_query_nearest(index, x, y, k = 1L, max_distance = Inf)

geo_join_box(index, y, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

Arguments

index

A zugeo_index.

extent

A geo_extent.

x, y

Query coordinates for geo_query_radius() and geo_query_nearest().

r

The radius.

k

The most neighbours to return.

max_distance

The largest box distance to return.

lossy

As for geo_box().

Value

For geo_query_box() and geo_query_radius(), an integer vector or a data frame of query and row. For geo_query_nearest(), a data frame of query, row and distance. For geo_join_box(), a data frame of x (positions in the indexed vector) and y.

Details

A query of one box or point gives the matching positions as a sorted integer vector; several give a data frame of query and row.

Examples

x <- geo_points(c(0, 5, 9), c(0, 5, 9))
tree <- geo_rtree(x)
geo_query_nearest(tree, 4, 4, k = 2)
#>   query row distance
#> 1     1   2 1.414214
#> 2     1   1 5.656854
geo_join_box(tree, geo_extent(c(-1, 8), c(-1, 8), c(1, 10), c(1, 10)))
#>   x y
#> 1 1 1
#> 2 3 2
